label: Queue
description: What a data graph asks of a broker: put a message on a queue, and prepare what the broker needs to keep one. Both are effects, listed under a feature's effects and stubbed by a rehearsal, so nothing leaves the process until the tree is served.

publish.description: Put one message on a queue of a broker: the body is the message, of the edge type `type` names, and the headers ride beside it, where a credential for the consuming trigger's policies goes. A queue trigger of this tree that consumes the same connection and queue must accept that type (X403). Answers the broker's id for the message. Inside an atomic graph it takes part in the transaction where the connection's kind is marked storage: the queue is kept in the store, and the message exists exactly when the graph's writes commit. A broker of any other kind cannot join, and X405 refuses the atomic graph.

connection.description: a connection document whose kind declares delivery: the broker

queue.description: the queue's name on that broker

type.description: the edge type of the message; a shape with no blob field at any depth, since a blob's handle is process-local (X404)

message.description: the message body, written in place or read from a node

headers.description: what rides beside the body, by name; the consuming trigger reads them as request.headers

delayMs.description: how long the message is held before it may be delivered, in milliseconds; absent: at once

id.description: the broker's id for the message, which the consuming trigger reads as request.id

ensure.description: Create what the broker needs to keep queues on this connection -- a table, say -- and never alter what exists; a broker that needs nothing does nothing. A startup step reaches it through a domain port bound to a data graph, so what a tree prepares is what its project.json says it prepares.

connection.description: a connection document whose kind declares delivery: the broker

ready.description: true once the broker can keep queues on the connection
